author: ViceTechnicolour
body:
Heads up: Download MCEdit-Unified on the official site here. If you have the older MCEdit or any other versions of MCEdit, they may conflict and MCEdit will not open. It is recommended to delete any pre-existing MCEdit if you are installing in the same directory. As well as this, this tutorial is done in Windows, however the MCEdit program should be the same across multiple operating systems.

I am not personally responsible for any loss of your world. Please make a backup before you follow this tutorial, just in case. You can clone worlds in singleplayer, or copy and paste your world from the saves folder in .minecraft to create a secondary copy.

Pruning is an essential key component when it comes to releasing & submitting your map. It should be the absolute last thing you do, so once it reopens no further chunks regenerate, the world size balloons, and you have to repeat the process over again. Pruning is a process on a majority of the current maps: I will show you a basic tutorial on how to prune your map.


Steps on Pruning a Map



1: Open MCEdit (once installed, however installing is quick and painless.)
2: Press TAB and go into Chunk View (or click the "Chunk View" at the top.)


NOTE: Your map should look like this currently.

3: Use your left mouse button to make a point, then drag the region over the boundaries of your map. Zoom in as necessary, to get a more concise prune. You should have a gray box that covers every block of your map, from one end to the other.

NOTE: Your map should look like this currently.

4: If it isn't already selected, go to the Chunk icon in your bottom bar that says "Chunk Control". 


5: A menu should pop up to the left of your screen giving you the following options:
- Deselect
- Create
- Delete
- Prune
- Relight
- Repop
- Don't Repop

You should first click the "Relight" option, so there are no lighting errors.


6: Wait for it to finish processing, then click "Prune". You should have this description:


7: Once clicked, confirm that you want to prune it and your map will be cleaned up. SAVE the world with CTRL+S. Feel free to then upload the map as you wish, packaging it with a map.png, map_banner.png, map.xml, level.dat, and the region files that came with it. Keep in mind, once you prune a map it cannot be reverted. The files are deleted permanently off your disk.



Your selection should be the only thing that has a checkerboard pattern, everything else should be void and distinguished as a greenish color. Once this is completed, you're all set and you may feel free to set up a download.
